title: Introduce typed presubmit profiles and compact release dry-run prober
author: Liam Chen
description: Motivation: Our presubmit matrix has grown organic profiles encoded in bash + make targets. That makes on-call triage and staged fastpaths brittle and hard to reason about. This PR introduces a typed presubmit profile abstraction implemented as a small TypeScript action and a compact release dry-run prober that exercises release hooks without performing real deploys. Goals: 1) standardize presubmit profiles (fast, full, infra-smoke) as typed JSON schema so CI can select lightweight lanes deterministically, 2) replace ad-hoc shell scripts with a single typed action to reduce flakiness and enable incremental test-slicing, 3) add a non-invasive release dry-run prober to validate release choreographies and ensure that release automation hooks (signing, artifact promotion, rollback policies) are runnable in CI without impacting production. Design summary: - presubmit profiles: schema v1 under .github/presubmit/profiles.schema.ts and profiles/ directory with canonical profiles. Profiles are validated at PR time by the new action .github/actions/typed-presubmit. - typed action: small node-based action (TS compiled) that resolves changed paths, maps to profile buckets, and emits annotations consistent with our existing presubmit telemetry. The action supports a --dry-run mode used by local devcontainers. - release dry-run prober: lightweight Go binary under ci/probers/release_dryrun that simulates release hooks (artifact signing stub, permission checks, rollout-fallback path) against a mocked control-plane. The prober runs as part of a staged release-check job and produces structured JSON reports which are then stored as artifacts for later inspection. Implementation notes: - Migration path: legacy make targets still work; a temporary compatibility shim maps old target names to profiles for two weeks before deprecation. - Rollout: gated behind a feature flag in CI config (ci/flags.yaml) and will be flipped after two successful nightly runs. - Performance: end-to-end presubmit latency for incremental changes reduced on average by 22% in internal experiments by skipping heavyweight E2E in fast profile. - Safety: the release dry-run uses mocked signing and does not touch production credentials; integration tests verify no network calls to production endpoints. Why not a monolithic refactor: typed action is intentionally tiny (approx 280 LOC) to make future audits easier. Follow-ups: create a presubmit-dashboard card (ENG-10235) to visualize profile distributions. Backcompat: none for external consumers. This long description contains context, motivation, implementation details, rollout plan, and follow-up work in one continuous string per repo conventions.

release_notes: Introduce typed presubmit profiles to standardize and speed CI presubmit selection.
Add a compact release dry-run prober to validate release hooks without production side effects.
Reduce incremental presubmit latency for common code changes by ~22%.
Backward-compatible compatibility shim for legacy Make targets; removal planned after two weeks.
